CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in both hands.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 60-year-old right-handed male who presents with numbness and tingling in both hands for a few weeks, beginning after a car wreck in December when he broke both wrists. Symptoms became more noticeable once the wrists healed and have worsened over the last month. Right wrist is more symptomatic than left. Patient wears splints on both wrists, predominantly on the right, which provides some relief. On the right side, symptoms extend from the middle and ring finger up the forearm. On the left side, symptoms extend from the pinky and ring finger. Patient describes mainly soreness with occasional throbbing and associated weakness when using the hands. Tingling is more pronounced when pain is present and becomes dull when pain subsides. Symptoms are worse at night and come and go throughout the day. Patient denies loss of sensation but notes hands may be less sensitive than normal. He has been prescribed nerve pain medicine but is not taking it as prescribed. Patient also reports mild stiffness in the neck after hitting his head during the accident; he was told it was a contusion.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: fatigue and weight gain. GI: excessive appetite and bloating. Eyes: floaters. Cardiovascular: shortness of breath and leg swelling. Endocrine: always hungry. Skin: nail bed changes, dryness, and itching. Musculoskeletal: gout and muscle pain. Remainder of review of systems: negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Car wreck in December with bilateral wrist fractures and head contusion. Prediabetes, controlled with diet. Hypertension. Anxiety. Denies history of thyroid issues.

MEDICATIONS
Coreg for hypertension. Lexapro for anxiety. Nerve pain medicine (not taking as prescribed).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Right-handed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination: Sensation normal except pin prick sensation diminished in third and fourth fingers on right and sensation decreased in fourth and fifth fingers on left. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities; 2+ in knees; toes downgoing bilaterally. Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows. Rest of exam normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome is most likely diagnosis, though bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome is also possible. Nerve irritation in wrists appears aggravated by past trauma. Schedule patient for EMG test to pinpoint location of nerve irritation. Follow-up visit after test completion. If symptoms persist, consider referral to hand clinic for injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedist for same treatment options. Continue wearing splints.
